Dynamical screening of the magnetic component of the QED and QCD one-gluon-exchange interaction leads to an enhancement of the energy loss of fast partons in a quark- gluon plasma.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methods of analysis of experimental data on heavy ion collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) and the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in the context of the Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP).
the study of radiated gluons and quanta in a hot QED and QCD medium, with emphasis on the role of dynamical screening in the one-gluonic interaction.
the study of the dynamical screening of the magnetic component of the QCD interaction, which has been neglected so far, in the radiative energy loss in a QCD plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiative parton-energy-loss mechanism in a hot QED plasma is not very different from the case of a QCD plasma.
radiative energy loss in a hot QED plasma is larger than in a QCD plasma.
the radiative energy loss in a hot QED or QCD plasma is about twice as big as when only the perturbative electric part of the one gluon exchange is considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a parton propagating in a hot QED matter would lose more energy than in a hot QGP.
the radiative parton-energy-loss is enhanced in a quark gluon plasma by about a factor of 2.
the magnetic interaction in a quark gluon plasma is as strong as that in a vacuum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of the magnetic interaction is essential in order to obtain a realistic estimate of the energy loss in a QGP.
the magnetic screening mass plays a significant role in the radiative energy loss and mean-free-path of a fast partons inside a hot QCD medium.
the magnetic component of the one-guon exchange interaction is as important as the electric component in determining the radiative energy loss and the mean-free-path in the quark-gluom plasma.
